name: The Mess Hall
firstVisit: Noise hits you like a door. Clattering, shouting, chewing.
So this is where everyone is.

W: Stone, with dents in it at fist height. Hundreds of them. Some are fresh.
1: Back to the Great Hall, where it's quiet. Suspiciously quiet, now you know where everyone is.
5: 3. Whatever is left is for the strong.
R: The same name, chalked in fresh every morning for nine years: BRUNO.
Underneath, smaller: TODAY'S SECOND STRONGEST EATER: BRUNO'S BROTHER (RETIRED).
F: A great hearth, a cauldron of porridge hung over it. It's been bubbling since before you were born.
It may be the same porridge.
c: A torch. Somebody has hung a sausage over it to cook. It has been hanging there a very long time.
m: The serving counter, scarred with knife marks. Every soldier gets one ladle. The strong get two.
Nobody has ever been brave enough to ask for a third.
q: Two barrels. One says WATER. The other says ALSO WATER.
The king doesn't hold with ale. The soldiers hold with the second barrel.
t: A long table, scored with dents the shape of forearms.
Arm-wrestling isn't allowed at meals. Meals aren't allowed to stop arm-wrestling.
r: A rack for leaving your weapons at the door. It's empty. Everyone's weapons are at the table, being eaten next to.

objects.name: Cook Hulda
lines: Porridge. You want porridge. Everyone wants porridge. There is only porridge.
Strength porridge. It's the same as the other porridge, but I shout at it.

answer: Oats. Iron filings, for the iron. Raw eggs, for the... eggs.
And a pinch of salt. I'm not a monster.
Bruno. Nine years running. Nobody's come close.
His brother came close, once. We don't talk about it. He's fine. He's mostly fine. He doesn't eat porridge any more.
You? Show me your arms.
...Half a bowl. And you sit at the end. The end is for arms like those.
It IS boot. Tuesday is boot.
Oh, you meant the smell. Out of my kitchen.

questions.ask: How long have you two been at it?
answer: Since breakfast.
HARRICK: Since Tuesday.
Since Tuesday's breakfast.
Strength is everything. The king says so.
HARRICK: Whoever wins gets the last bread roll.
...Strength is everything, and there's a bread roll.

questions.ask: Want me to take on the winner?
answer: Ha!
HARRICK: Ha!
...Neither of us can let go. Our hands went to sleep on Wednesday. Could you fetch somebody?
WHAT.
HARRICK: WHAT.
* They both let go at once to get up and hit you, and both fall straight over. Their arms have been asleep since Wednesday.
...Best of three.

objects.name: Corporal Harrick
lines: Don't talk to him. He's losing.

objects.name: Bruno
lines: (He holds up one finger: one moment. Forty minutes later, he's still holding it up. He's still eating.)
